import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Komi

In the game of Go, *komi* is the number of points added to White's score to compensate for
Black moving first. A *perfect* komi is a value that makes the game end in a draw (*jigo*) under
perfect play by both sides. Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks:

> What is the perfect value of komi?

The answer depends on the ruleset, which the source does not fix. We use the Tromp–Taylor rules,
a complete and precise ruleset with area scoring: stones are placed on the empty points of a
square grid; after a move, first the opponent's and then one's own stones without liberties are
removed; a move may not recreate an earlier grid colouring (positional superko); the game ends
after two consecutive passes; a player's score is the number of points of their colour plus the
number of empty points that reach only their colour. We also allow the variant in which suicide
(a move that removes one's own stones) is forbidden, as in most other area scoring rulesets.

Under perfect play, Black can force a final score margin of at least some value $V$, and White
can force a margin of at most $V$; this minimax value $V$ (an integer) is the perfect komi:
with komi $V$ perfect play ends in *jigo*, with any other komi one side can force a win.
Under area scoring, statistics from professional and computer play suggest that the perfect komi
is $7$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Komi (Go)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komi_%28Go%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [J. Tromp, B. Taylor, The logical rules of Go](https://tromp.github.io/go.html)
-/

def Chain (p q : Point n) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => (grid n).Adj a b ∧ pos b = pos p) p q
blocks.docstring:
`pos.Chain p q` holds if `q` can be reached from `p` by a path of adjacent points all of
the same colour as `p`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.Reachable`/`induce` (Chain is `Relation.ReflTransGen` on a colour-restricted adjacency, which is simpler to use); nothing in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib models Go captures or scoring.

def Reaches (p : Point n) (c : Option Color) : Prop :=
  pos p ≠ c ∧ ∃ q r, pos.Chain p q ∧ (grid n).Adj q r ∧ pos r = c
blocks.docstring:

blocks.name: IsLegal
blocks.text:
/-- Playing at `p` is legal if `p` is empty, the resulting position has not occurred before
(positional superko) and, unless suicide is allowed, the played stone is not removed. -/
def IsLegal (r : Rules) (s : State n) (p : Point n) : Prop :=
  s.pos p = none ∧ s.pos.play s.toMove p ∉ s.history ∧
    (r.suicideAllowed ∨ s.pos.play s.toMove p p = some s.toMove)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def options (r : Rules) (s : State n) : Finset (State n) :=
  insert s.pass ((Finset.univ.filter (s.IsLegal r)).image s.move)
blocks.docstring: The states that can be reached in one turn: by passing or by a legal move.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem measure_lt_of_mem_options {r : Rules} {s t : State n} (ht : t ∈ s.options r)
    (hs : ¬ s.IsTerminal) : t.measure < s.measure := by
  simp only [IsTerminal, not_le] at hs
  simp only [options, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at ht
  obtain rfl | ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ := ht
  · simp only [measure, pass]
    omega
  · have h₁ := Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hp.2.1
    have h₂ := Finset.card_le_univ (insert (s.pos.play s.toMove p) s.history)
    simp only [measure, move]
    omega
blocks.docstring: Every turn of a game that has not ended decreases `measure`.

  simp only [options, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at ht
  obtain rfl | ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ := ht
  · simp only [measure, pass]
    omega
  · have h₁ := Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hp.2.1

blocks.code:
noncomputable def value (r : Rules) (s : State n) : ℤ :=
  if s.IsTerminal then s.pos.margin
  else
    have hne : (s.options r).attach.Nonempty :=
      Finset.attach_nonempty_iff.2 ⟨_, s.pass_mem_options r⟩
    if s.toMove = .black then
      (s.options r).attach.sup' hne fun t => value r t.1
    else
      (s.options r).attach.inf' hne fun t => value r t.1
termination_by s.measure
decreasing_by all_goals exact measure_lt_of_mem_options t.2 ‹_›

/-- The minimax value, from state `s`, of Black's final score margin: Black maximises it and
White minimises it. -/
noncomputable def value (r : Rules) (s : State n) : ℤ :=
  if s.IsTerminal then s.pos.margin

@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem perfectKomi_size_one (b : Bool) : perfectKomi { size := 1, suicideAllowed := b } = 0 := by
  -- no two points of a `1 × 1` board are adjacent, so nothing reaches anything
  have hR (pos : Position 1) (p : Point 1) (c : Option Color) : ¬ pos.Reaches p c :=
    fun ⟨_, q, r, _, h, _⟩ => h.ne (Subsingleton.elim q r)
  -- hence a stone played on the board is removed at once
  have hplay (pos : Position 1) (c : Color) (p : Point 1) : pos.play c p = fun _ => none := by
    funext q
    obtain rfl : q = p := Subsingleton.elim q p
    simp [Position.play, Position.clear, hR]
  -- so the only possible turn is to pass
  have hopt (s : State 1) (hs : (fun _ => none) ∈ s.history) :
      s.options { size := 1, suicideAllowed := b } = {s.pass} := by
    have hleg (p : Point 1) : ¬ s.IsLegal { size := 1, suicideAllowed := b } p :=
      fun ⟨_, h, _⟩ => h (by rw [hplay]; exact hs)
    classical
    rw [State.options, Finset.filter_false_of_mem fun p _ => hleg p, Finset.image_empty,
      Finset.insert_empty]
  have h0 : (fun _ => none) ∈ (State.initial 1).history := by simp [State.initial]
  rw [perfectKomi, State.value_eq_of_options_eq_singleton (by decide) (hopt _ h0),
    State.value_eq_of_options_eq_singleton (by decide) (hopt (State.initial 1).pass h0),
    State.value, if_pos (by decide)]
  simp [State.initial, State.pass, Position.margin, Position.score, hR]

claims.decomposer_note: The article defines perfect komi as the value making a 19x19 Go game end in jigo under perfect play (i.e. the minimax value of the game, Black's final score margin) and asserts the candidate answer 7 (under area scoring, where without seki the value is claimed to be an odd integer), so the Prop is 'the perfect komi equals 7'; the value depends on the ruleset (area vs territory scoring, seki, ko/superko rule) and formalizing it requires a full formal model of Go, and the repository's usual shape for such value problems is `value = answer(sorry)` with 7 as the candidate.
claims.reviewer_why: c06 gives a complete, literal transcription of the Tromp–Taylor rules (reach with the 'not coloured C' guard, simultaneous clearing, opponent then own colour, positional superko with history including the initial and current colouring, two consecutive passes end the game, area scoring), a well-founded minimax with proved termination and no fuel/default values, a proved 1×1 sanity test, and a `Rules` structure that lets the main statement use canonical Tromp–Taylor (suicide allowed) while a variant states the no-suicide (Chinese/AGA-style) version. Main declaration is `perfectKomi .trompTaylor = answer(sorry)` (question form, per CONTRIBUTING), with `komi.variants.eq_seven` recording the article's suggested value 7 and `komi.variants.no_suicide` hedging the ruleset choice. c04/c05/c07 are essentially equivalent models but each fixes only one suicide convention (c07 forbids suicide, departing from Tromp–Taylor without a variant); c01 uses a fuel-based recursion with hand-rolled adjacency and hard-codes `= 7` as the sole statement instead of `answer(sorry)`. My edits to c06: `Position` made an `abbrev` (dropping the manual instances), copyright year, and minor docstring wording (explicitly noting the source does not fix a ruleset). Additional sanity proofs I ran separately (liberty detection, clearing, capture on a 2×2 board) behave as expected.

context:
Komi (込み, コミ) in the game of Go are points added to the score of the player with the white stones as compensation for playing second. The value of Black's first-move advantage is generally considered to be between 5 and 7 points by the end of the game.
Standard komi is 6.5 points under the Japanese and Korean rules; under Chinese, Ing and AGA rules standard komi is 7.5 points; under New Zealand rules standard komi is 7 points. Komi typically applies only to games where both players are evenly ranked. In the case of a one-rank difference, the stronger player will typically play with the white stones and players often agree on a simple 0.5-point komi to break a tie (jigo) in favour of white, or no komi at all. Komidashi (コミ出し) is the more complete Japanese language term.  The Chinese term is tiē mù (simplified Chinese: 贴目; traditional Chinese: 貼目) and the Korean term is deom (덤).
Efforts have been made to determine the value of komi for boards much smaller than the standard 19x19 grid for go, such as 7x7. When introducing Environmental Go, Elwyn Berlekamp made a broad generalisation of komi to illustrate the practical value of the temperature concept from combinatorial game theory.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Komi

In the game of Go, *komi* is the number of points added to White's score to compensate for
Black moving first. A *perfect* komi is a value that makes the game end in a draw (*jigo*) under
perfect play by both sides. Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks:

> What is the perfect value of komi?

The answer depends on the ruleset, which the source does not fix. We use the Tromp–Taylor rules,
a complete and precise ruleset with area scoring: stones are placed on the empty points of a
square grid; after a move, first the opponent's and then one's own stones without liberties are
removed; a move may not recreate an earlier grid colouring (positional superko); the game ends
after two consecutive passes; a player's score is the number of points of their colour plus the
number of empty points that reach only their colour. We also allow the variant in which suicide
(a move that removes one's own stones) is forbidden, as in most other area scoring rulesets.

Under perfect play, Black can force a final score margin of at least some value $V$, and White
can force a margin of at most $V$; this minimax value $V$ (an integer) is the perfect komi:
with komi $V$ perfect play ends in *jigo*, with any other komi one side can force a win.
Under area scoring, statistics from professional and computer play suggest that the perfect komi
is $7$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Komi (Go)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komi_%28Go%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [J. Tromp, B. Taylor, The logical rules of Go](https://tromp.github.io/go.html)
-/

namespace Komi

/-- The two players, identified with the colour of their stones. -/
inductive Color
  | black
  | white
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The opponent of a player. -/
def Color.opp : Color → Color
  | black => white
  | white => black

/-- The points of an `n × n` Go board. -/
abbrev Point (n : ℕ) := Fin n × Fin n

/-- The grid graph of the board: two points are adjacent if they are horizontal or vertical
neighbours. -/
abbrev grid (n : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Point n) :=
  SimpleGraph.pathGraph n □ SimpleGraph.pathGraph n

/-- A position colours each point of the board black, white or empty (`none`). -/
abbrev Position (n : ℕ) := Point n → Option Color

namespace Position

variable {n : ℕ} (pos : Position n)

/-- `pos.Chain p q` holds if `q` can be reached from `p` by a path of adjacent points all of
the same colour as `p`. -/
def Chain (p q : Point n) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => (grid n).Adj a b ∧ pos b = pos p) p q

/-- A point `p` not coloured `c` *reaches* `c` if there is a path of adjacent points of `p`'s
colour from `p` to a point of colour `c`. -/
def Reaches (p : Point n) (c : Option Color) : Prop :=
  pos p ≠ c ∧ ∃ q r, pos.Chain p q ∧ (grid n).Adj q r ∧ pos r = c

open scoped Classical in
/-- Clearing a colour `c`: emptying all points of colour `c` that do not reach empty. -/
noncomputable def clear (c : Color) : Position n :=
  fun p => if pos p = some c ∧ ¬ pos.Reaches p none then none else pos p

/-- The position obtained when player `c` plays at the point `p`: colour `p` with `c`, then clear
the opponent's colour, then clear one's own colour. -/
noncomputable def play (c : Color) (p : Point n) : Position n :=
  (Position.clear (Function.update pos p (some c)) c.opp).clear c

open scoped Classical in
/-- The (area) score of player `c`: the number of points of colour `c` plus the number of empty
points that reach only colour `c`. -/
noncomputable def score (c : Color) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun p => pos p = some c ∨
    (pos p = none ∧ pos.Reaches p (some c) ∧ ¬ pos.Reaches p (some c.opp))).card

/-- Black's score minus White's score. -/
noncomputable def margin : ℤ :=
  pos.score .black - pos.score .white

end Position

/-- The parameters of the ruleset: the side length of the board, and whether suicide (a move
that removes one's own stones) is allowed. -/
structure Rules where
  /-- The side length of the (square) board. -/
  size : ℕ
  /-- Whether a move that removes one's own stones is allowed. -/
  suicideAllowed : Bool

/-- The Tromp–Taylor rules on the standard `19 × 19` board; suicide is allowed. -/
def Rules.trompTaylor : Rules where
  size := 19
  suicideAllowed := true

/-- The state of a game: the current position, the player to move, the set of all positions
that have occurred so far (including the current one) and the number of consecutive passes
that have just been made. -/
structure State (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The current position. -/
  pos : Position n
  /-- The player to move. -/
  toMove : Color
  /-- All positions that have occurred so far, including the current one. -/
  history : Finset (Position n)
  /-- The number of consecutive passes immediately preceding this state. -/
  passes : ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq

namespace State

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The initial state: the empty board, Black to move. -/
def initial (n : ℕ) : State n where
  pos := fun _ => none
  toMove := .black
  history := {fun _ => none}
  passes := 0

/-- The game ends after two consecutive passes. -/
def IsTerminal (s : State n) : Prop := 2 ≤ s.passes

instance (s : State n) : Decidable s.IsTerminal := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (2 ≤ s.passes))

/-- The state after the player to move passes. -/
def pass (s : State n) : State n :=
  { s with toMove := s.toMove.opp, passes := s.passes + 1 }

/-- The state after the player to move plays at `p`. -/
noncomputable def move (s : State n) (p : Point n) : State n where
  pos := s.pos.play s.toMove p
  toMove := s.toMove.opp
  history := insert (s.pos.play s.toMove p) s.history
  passes := 0

/-- Playing at `p` is legal if `p` is empty, the resulting position has not occurred before
(positional superko) and, unless suicide is allowed, the played stone is not removed. -/
def IsLegal (r : Rules) (s : State n) (p : Point n) : Prop :=
  s.pos p = none ∧ s.pos.play s.toMove p ∉ s.history ∧
    (r.suicideAllowed ∨ s.pos.play s.toMove p p = some s.toMove)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The states that can be reached in one turn: by passing or by a legal move. -/
noncomputable def options (r : Rules) (s : State n) : Finset (State n) :=
  insert s.pass ((Finset.univ.filter (s.IsLegal r)).image s.move)

/-- A measure that decreases along every turn of a game that has not ended. -/
def measure (s : State n) : ℕ :=
  2 * (Fintype.card (Position n) - s.history.card) + (2 - s.passes)

/-- Passing is always an option. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem pass_mem_options (r : Rules) (s : State n) : s.pass ∈ s.options r :=
  Finset.mem_insert_self _ _

/-- Every turn of a game that has not ended decreases `measure`. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem measure_lt_of_mem_options {r : Rules} {s t : State n} (ht : t ∈ s.options r)
    (hs : ¬ s.IsTerminal) : t.measure < s.measure := by
  simp only [IsTerminal, not_le] at hs
  simp only [options, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at ht
  obtain rfl | ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ := ht
  · simp only [measure, pass]
    omega
  · have h₁ := Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hp.2.1
    have h₂ := Finset.card_le_univ (insert (s.pos.play s.toMove p) s.history)
    simp only [measure, move]
    omega

/-- The minimax value, from state `s`, of Black's final score margin: Black maximises it and
White minimises it. -/
noncomputable def value (r : Rules) (s : State n) : ℤ :=
  if s.IsTerminal then s.pos.margin
  else
    have hne : (s.options r).attach.Nonempty :=
      Finset.attach_nonempty_iff.2 ⟨_, s.pass_mem_options r⟩
    if s.toMove = .black then
      (s.options r).attach.sup' hne fun t => value r t.1
    else
      (s.options r).attach.inf' hne fun t => value r t.1
termination_by s.measure
decreasing_by all_goals exact measure_lt_of_mem_options t.2 ‹_›

end State

/-- The perfect komi under the rules `r`: the minimax value of Black's final score margin from
the empty board with Black to move. With this komi, perfect play by both sides ends in *jigo*. -/
noncomputable def perfectKomi (r : Rules) : ℤ :=
  State.value r (State.initial r.size)

/-- If passing is the only option, the value is the value after passing. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem State.value_eq_of_options_eq_singleton {n : ℕ} {r : Rules} {s : State n}
    (hs : ¬ s.IsTerminal) (h : s.options r = {s.pass}) : s.value r = s.pass.value r := by
  rw [State.value, if_neg hs]
  have hsub : ∀ t : {x // x ∈ s.options r}, t.1 = s.pass := fun t =>
    Finset.mem_singleton.1 (by rw [← h]; exact t.2)
  split_ifs
  · exact le_antisymm (Finset.sup'_le _ _ fun t _ => by rw [hsub t])
      (Finset.le_sup' (f := fun t : {x // x ∈ s.options r} => t.1.value r)
        (b := ⟨s.pass, s.pass_mem_options r⟩) (Finset.mem_attach _ _))
  · exact le_antisymm
      (Finset.inf'_le (f := fun t : {x // x ∈ s.options r} => t.1.value r)
        (b := ⟨s.pass, s.pass_mem_options r⟩) (Finset.mem_attach _ _))
      (Finset.le_inf' _ _ fun t _ => by rw [hsub t])

/-- On a `1 × 1` board no stone can ever be played, so both players pass and the perfect komi
is `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem perfectKomi_size_one (b : Bool) : perfectKomi { size := 1, suicideAllowed := b } = 0 := by
  -- no two points of a `1 × 1` board are adjacent, so nothing reaches anything
  have hR (pos : Position 1) (p : Point 1) (c : Option Color) : ¬ pos.Reaches p c :=
    fun ⟨_, q, r, _, h, _⟩ => h.ne (Subsingleton.elim q r)
  -- hence a stone played on the board is removed at once
  have hplay (pos : Position 1) (c : Color) (p : Point 1) : pos.play c p = fun _ => none := by
    funext q
    obtain rfl : q = p := Subsingleton.elim q p
    simp [Position.play, Position.clear, hR]
  -- so the only possible turn is to pass
  have hopt (s : State 1) (hs : (fun _ => none) ∈ s.history) :
      s.options { size := 1, suicideAllowed := b } = {s.pass} := by
    have hleg (p : Point 1) : ¬ s.IsLegal { size := 1, suicideAllowed := b } p :=
      fun ⟨_, h, _⟩ => h (by rw [hplay]; exact hs)
    classical
    rw [State.options, Finset.filter_false_of_mem fun p _ => hleg p, Finset.image_empty,
      Finset.insert_empty]
  have h0 : (fun _ => none) ∈ (State.initial 1).history := by simp [State.initial]
  rw [perfectKomi, State.value_eq_of_options_eq_singleton (by decide) (hopt _ h0),
    State.value_eq_of_options_eq_singleton (by decide) (hopt (State.initial 1).pass h0),
    State.value, if_pos (by decide)]
  simp [State.initial, State.pass, Position.margin, Position.score, hR]

/--
What is the perfect value of komi? That is, under the Tromp–Taylor rules on the standard
`19 × 19` board, what is the minimax value of Black's final score margin, i.e. the komi with which
perfect play by both sides ends in *jigo*? Statistics from professional and computer play suggest
that the answer is $7$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem komi : perfectKomi .trompTaylor = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Statistics from professional and computer play suggest that under area scoring the perfect komi
is $7$: under the Tromp–Taylor rules on the standard `19 × 19` board, the minimax value of
Black's final score margin is $7$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem komi.variants.eq_seven : perfectKomi .trompTaylor = 7 := by
  sorry

/--
What is the perfect value of komi on the standard `19 × 19` board under the Tromp–Taylor rules
modified to forbid suicide (as the Chinese and AGA rules do)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem komi.variants.no_suicide :
    perfectKomi { size := 19, suicideAllowed := false } = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Komi

items: Ruleset: the informal statement does not fix rules; following the article (which attributes the candidate value 7 to area scoring), the main statement uses the Tromp–Taylor rules (https://tromp.github.io/go.html): 19×19 board, Black first, area scoring, positional superko (a move may not recreate any earlier position, including the initial empty board and the current one), suicide allowed, game ends after two consecutive passes. A `Rules` structure with fields `size : ℕ` and `suicideAllowed : Bool` is used so the no-suicide variant (Chinese/AGA-style) can be stated as `komi.variants.no_suicide`. Territory (Japanese) scoring and situational superko are NOT modelled.

Perfect komi is defined as the minimax value V (in ℤ) of Black's final score margin (Black's area score minus White's): Black can force margin ≥ V and White can force ≤ V, so komi V is the unique komi with which perfect play yields jigo; any other komi lets one side force a win. This is the reading of 'perfect komi makes each game result in jigo under perfect play' from the article. Hence the answer type is ℤ (half-integer komis can never be perfect).

Minimax is defined by well-founded recursion on `State.measure = 2*(#positions − #history) + (2 − passes)`; termination is proved (`measure_lt_of_mem_options`), so no fuel/default values are involved. Black takes `Finset.sup'`, White `Finset.inf'` over the options (pass is always an option, giving nonemptiness). At a terminal state (two consecutive passes) the value is the margin regardless of whose turn it is.

Tromp–Taylor primitives are transcribed literally: `Reaches p c` = path of points of p's colour from p to a point adjacent to a point of colour c (with the 'p not coloured c' guard); `clear c` empties simultaneously all points of colour c not reaching empty; `play` = place stone on an empty point, clear opponent, then clear own colour; `score c` = points of colour c plus empty points reaching only colour c. Adjacency is the Mathlib grid graph `pathGraph n □ pathGraph n` (orthogonal neighbours).

No-suicide variant: a move is illegal if the played stone is removed by the own-colour clearing (`play … p ≠ some toMove`); this is equivalent to 'no own stones are removed' because in play every chain has a liberty before the move.
Main declaration uses `answer(sorry)` (the statement is a question); the article's candidate value 7 is stated separately as `komi.variants.eq_seven : perfectKomi .trompTaylor = 7` (research open).

The `test` theorem `perfectKomi_size_one` (1×1 board ⇒ perfect komi 0) is fully proved, together with a small API lemma `State.value_eq_of_options_eq_singleton`; these serve as executable sanity checks of the bespoke definitions (as CONTRIBUTING.md requests for bespoke definitions).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity: the source ('What is the perfect value of Komi?') does not fix a ruleset, and the perfect komi depends on it (area vs territory scoring, superko variant, suicide). The bail-outs (c02, c03, c08) omit on that ground plus the absence of a Go model. I judged that fixing the canonical Tromp–Taylor logical rules (the standard precise area-scoring formulation, matching the article's 'under area scoring' remark) and documenting that choice in the module and theorem docstrings is a legitimate modeling decision, with precedent for in-file game models with minimax evaluators (Paper/CatchUpConjecture.lean). The no-suicide variant is included so the two common area-scoring suicide conventions are both stated; territory (Japanese) scoring and situational superko are not modelled. Perfect komi is formalised as the minimax value of Black's area margin (ℤ), which is exactly the unique komi that yields jigo under perfect play. The `= 7` variant records the article's statistics-based suggestion; the seki caveat (odd integer only in the absence of seki) does not affect the statements, which make no parity claim. The main slot uses `answer(sorry)` per repository convention for questions; the decomposition note calling the Prop 'perfect komi equals 7' is covered by `komi.variants.eq_seven`.
